slot.brief: Evaluate a sum like tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y by converting to an addition formula, checking the principal value branch.

stem: Evaluate $\tan^{-1}2+\tan^{-1}3$, where $\tan^{-1}$ takes its principal value.

verdicts.working: Both principal arctangents are in $(0,\pi/2)$, so their sum is in $(\pi/2,\pi)$. Its tangent is $(2+3)/(1-2\cdot3)=-1$, hence the sum is $3\pi/4$.

working:
Let $S=\tan^{-1}2+\tan^{-1}3$. Then $\tan S=\dfrac{2+3}{1-2\cdot3}=-1$. Since $S\in(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pi)$, $S=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.
